the BREATHER study has shown that a 5-day on/2-day off efavirenz based ART regimen is non-inferior in maintaining virological suppression to a 7-day on/0-day off regimen in a cohort of virologically-suppressed young people with HIV.

the study showed no evidence of virological failure with SCT over a median follow-up of 3.6yrs, with no evidence of increased risk of adverse events, but with a significantly higher rate of hospitalisation.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated that it is safe to take a break from antiretrovirals every weekend in young people who have had a good response to antiretrovirally treatment for 2-4 years.
we showed that short-cycle therapy (5 days on, two days off ART) can be sustained for up to 3.5 years with no difference in virological suppression when compared to continuous ART.
we showed that it is possible to take a break from antiretrovials in HIV positive young people without compromising virological suppression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have shown that short cycle therapy, where you take your antiretrovirus for 5 days a week and then you have 2 days off, is as good as continuous treatment.
it is feasible to take a 2-day weekend break from HIV treatment every week, with no increase in viral rebound.
it is safe to take a 2 day weekend off ART every week.
